subject: Help to write a model: simple linear regression with another regression on scale parameter

messages.author: 8b7d388508785c8c
messages.subject: Help to write a model: simple linear regression with another regression on scale parameter
parts:
Hi everyone,

I would like to write a linear regression with another regression on the scale parameter.

I've written this model but i am not sure about it: 

  data {
    int < lower = 0 > n_obs;   //number of observations
    real x[n_obs]; //Aggregation value
    real Y[n_obs]; //Residuals of Stock_Recruitment model
  }
  
  parameters {
    real intercept;
    real alpha; 
    real beta; 
    real intercept_sigma;
    real<lower = 0> sigma_sigma;
    real<lower = 0> sigma;
  }

  model {
    real mu[n_obs];
    real mu_sigma[n_obs];

    // Priors : 
    alpha ~ uniform(-5,5);
    beta ~ uniform(-5,5);
    intercept ~ uniform(-5,5);
    intercept_sigma ~ uniform(-5, 5);
    sigma_sigma ~ uniform(0.0001, 10);

    // Likelihood: 
      for(i in 1: n_obs) {
        mu_sigma[i] = intercept_sigma + beta * x[i]; 

        mu[i] = intercept + alpha * (x[i])  ;

        sigma ~ lognormal((mu_sigma[i]), sigma_sigma); 
        Y[i] ~ normal((mu[i]), sigma); 
      }
  } 


If i just write this : 
mu[i] = intercept + alpha * (x[i])  ;
mu_sigma[i] = intercept_sigma + beta * x[i]; 
Y[i] ~ normal((mu[i]), mu_sigma[i]); 

the model computes iterations with mu_sigma < 0. This is why i would to have sigma ~ lognormal((mu_sigma[i]), sigma_sigma).

Can you help me ? 

Thanks in advance,
Colin Bouchard

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Help to write a model: simple linear regression with another regression on scale parameter
parts:
On Oct 11, 2016, at 3:59 AM, Colin Bouchard <colin.b...@live.fr> wrote:
>
>
> Hi everyone,
>
> I would like to write a linear regression with another regression on the scale parameter.
>
> I've written this model but i am not sure about it:
>
> data {
> int < lower = 0 > n_obs; //number of observations
> real x[n_obs]; //Aggregation value
> real Y[n_obs]; //Residuals of Stock_Recruitment model
> }
>
> parameters {
> real intercept;
> real alpha;
> real beta;
> real intercept_sigma;
> real<lower = 0> sigma_sigma;
> real<lower = 0> sigma;
> }
>
> model {
> real mu[n_obs];
> real mu_sigma[n_obs];
>
> // Priors :
> alpha ~ uniform(-5,5);
> beta ~ uniform(-5,5);
> intercept ~ uniform(-5,5);
> intercept_sigma ~ uniform(-5, 5);

We strongly disrecommend these priors, but if you insist on using
them, you'll need to declare the relevant variables with constraints, e.g.,

real<lower=-5, upper=5> beta;

> sigma_sigma ~ uniform(0.0001, 10);

We disrecommend these 0.0001 lower-bounds, too --- either the data
will keep the distribution away from 0 or it'll all pile up at
0.0001. It's not likely to help in the way you think it might.

>
> // Likelihood:
> for(i in 1: n_obs) {
> mu_sigma[i] = intercept_sigma + beta * x[i];
>
> mu[i] = intercept + alpha * (x[i]) ;
>
> sigma ~ lognormal((mu_sigma[i]), sigma_sigma);
> Y[i] ~ normal((mu[i]), sigma);
> }
> }

That's OK. You do'nt need all those extra parens around x[i],
mu_sigma[i] and mu[i].

Setting

a ~ lognormal(m, s);

is the same as setting:

a_raw ~ normal(m, s);
a = exp(a_raw);

You can do it either way. The latter makes the (inverse) link function
for the positive-constrained regression explicit.

- Bob
